brief.subject: Dementia and firearm safety; what the midterms mean for Medicare
brief.headline: Experts Target Gun Safety as Dementia Emerges; Midterms Reopen Medicare Debate
brief.dek: Public health experts focus on firearm safety for older gun owners with cognitive decline, and a new Congress revives the Medicare for All question.
brief.lede: Public health experts are looking for ways to encourage safer firearm practices among older gun owners, especially when early signs of dementia appear.

sections.heading: Dementia and Guns at Home
bullets: Public health experts are developing approaches that encourage firearm safety among older adults who own guns.
The effort centers on households where a gun owner shows signs of cognitive decline, a situation many family caregivers face.
Families with concerns about a loved one's memory and home safety can raise the topic with that person's doctor.

sections.heading: Medicare for All Back in Play
bullets: Democrats took control of Congress in the midterms, helped by voter frustration over healthcare costs.
That shift has revived debate over Medicare for All, a key issue for current and future beneficiaries.
Democratic control does not guarantee Medicare for All will pass, despite hopes among some supporters.

brief.seo_description: Healthy Aging Brief: firearm safety for older gun owners showing signs of dementia, and what Democrats' midterm win means for Medicare for All.

items.title: When a Gun Owner Shows Early Signs of Dementia
items.snippet: Public health experts are finding ways to encourage firearm safety practices for older adults who own guns, especially when there are indications of cognitive decline.

items.title: Midterm Wave Sets a Course for ‘Medicare for All’ Fight
items.snippet: Voter frustration with healthcare costs helped fuel the Democrats’ midterm takeover of Congress. But Democratic control doesn’t mean “Medicare for All” will follow, as some hoped.
